item.title: Retake 1.0.26
item.description:
Fixes a regression in 1.0.25.

  • A region dragged with snapping on no longer flickers between its starting position and the snapped one while a snap guide is showing (RET-76).

item.title: Retake 1.0.25
item.description:
Fixes from a review of the editor, playback, recording and export code.

Timeline

Playback

Recording

Projects and export

  • Audio and camera takes that run past the end of the last screen clip now play and export. The picture holds its last frame under them and the timeline is greyed there. Previously they were cut off at the picture's end, which looked as though deleting a clip had cropped the narration (RET-64).
  • The volume, speed and zoom-amount lines only respond to a drag that goes up or down. A sideways drag from a line moves the item, as a drag beside the line does, so grabbing a clip by its middle no longer changes its volume (RET-66).
  • Recording a take or pasting with the playhead inside a freeze puts the clip in at the frozen frame; pasting several clips under a speed change keeps them together, and moves the audio after them by the right amount (RET-67).
  • With the timeline fitted, trimming the last clip no longer refits the zoom under the drag. An edge no longer sticks at its own starting position when a drag begins. A zoom, marker or speed change moved or dropped by a trim comes back when the trim is dragged back (RET-72).
  • Undo works for an edit repeated within a second of undoing it (RET-74).
  • The playhead no longer jumps to the start after an edit when the timeline is paused, jumped with Shift-←/→ or ↑/↓, or a recording, voiceover or export is started before the rebuilt player has settled. A new recording or voiceover started in that moment was placed at 0:00. Seeking or pausing during a mid-play rebuild now takes effect at once, and opening another project while playing starts it at its own playhead (RET-65).
  • A sideways swipe on the preview scrubs about one second per width and ignores the momentum after a flick.
  • A screen recording's camera follows speed changes and freezes (RET-73).
  • A capture that macOS stops on its own (the recorded window closed, a display unplugged) keeps what was recorded up to then instead of losing it, and the camera is released. A capture that fails to start leaves nothing running. A writer that fails (disk full, volume ejected) stops the recording with the reason (RET-68).
  • The frame round a window recording follows the window's real corner radius; it was about 3 points too tight (RET-75).
  • Opening, creating or closing a project, or exporting, while a voiceover is recording first stops and keeps the take (RET-69).
  • A recording that was undone no longer comes back when the project is reopened (RET-70).
  • Quitting during an export cancels it and removes the partial movie (RET-71).

item.title: Retake 1.0.24
item.description:
• Pause and resume are reliable. A screen recording that was paused and resumed could fail with "No frames were captured" when stopped. It is now kept, including when paused before the first frame.
  • Deleting clips keeps your audio. Deleting or cutting a screen clip no longer removes, trims or moves voiceovers, camera takes or music; only the screen clips close the gap.
  • Splitting a clip leaves a plain cut. The new cut has no transition and no fades; the clip's transitions and sound fades stay at its start and end.
  • Back to the start. After a voiceover, kept or discarded, the playhead returns to where it started.

item.title: Retake 1.0.23
item.description: • Pin or hide the inspector. A pin at the top of the inspector keeps it beside the editor. Unpin it and it slides away so the editor uses the whole window; click the strip on the window's right edge to slide it in, and click outside it to put it away.

item.title: Retake 1.0.22
item.description:
• Smooth playback while editing. Changing a speed change (or anything else that rebuilds the video) while playing no longer makes the playhead jump to the start or pause; playback carries straight on. The playhead also no longer steps back when you press play.
  • Markers stay on their frame. A marker marks a frame of the recording: adding, changing or deleting a speed change, or trimming, moving or deleting clips, moves it with that frame. A marker in a freeze frame keeps its place in the freeze.
  • The view is saved with the project. Where the timeline is scrolled to, how far it is zoomed, and the playhead are saved and restored when you open the project again.

item.title: Retake 1.0.21
item.description:
• Crossfades. Audio items that run into each other on the same lane now crossfade across the overlap instead of cutting over. The overlap is drawn with the two fade curves crossing.
  • Hear a trim. While dragging the edge of a voiceover, camera take or music item, press Space to hear the second of audio at the new edge; a small playhead follows it.
  • Freeze frames start and stop at once, with no easing. Other speed changes keep their easing.
  • Timeline locked while narrating. While a voiceover records, the timeline is dimmed and can't be edited, so nothing moves under the narration.

item.title: Retake 1.0.20
item.description:
• Hold the picture while you talk. While recording a voiceover, press ⇧Space (or click Hold Picture) to stop the video while your voice and camera keep recording, so you can finish a sentence. The preview shows PAUSED; Space or ⇧Space carries on. When the voiceover stops, each hold becomes a freeze frame on the Speed lane, so the narration stays in step with the picture.
  • Markers while narrating. Press M during a voiceover to add a marker at the playhead.

item.title: Retake 1.0.19
item.description: • Automatic updates. Retake now checks for new versions once a day and offers to install them; Retake › Check for Updates… checks straight away, and Check for Updates Automatically turns the daily check off. Updates are signed and verified before they are installed. Earlier versions don't check, so this version is installed by hand once; later versions are offered automatically.
